primary_source.title: Agent-First Tool APIs: Rethinking Enterprise Service Interfaces for LLM-Native Execution

end_to_end_table.paper_interpretation: The paper explicitly calls these +48.4% latency and +36.9% token consumption and says the reliability gains come at a measurable cost.

later_overhead_table.paper_interpretation: The later section explicitly says negative values are per-task savings after accounting for eliminated retry attempts and concludes Agent-First has lower per-task costs.

arithmetic_cross_check.relationship: The magnitudes in the later claimed savings equal the absolute magnitudes of the directly observed end-to-end increases but with opposite signs. The manuscript does not provide a reconciliation mapping Table III's per-task observed means to Table IX's net per-task values.

scope_correction: The contradiction is internal to the current v1 manuscript and is primary-source verified. It does not establish which economics number is correct. Without raw per-task logs, a corrected source, or an explicit derivation resolving the estimands, do not use either the -1.3 s/-680 token savings claim or a derived scheduler cost model that assumes those savings. The end-to-end Table III values remain direct reported measurements, but their provenance is still paper-level rather than raw-log independently replayed.
safe_downstream_use: Use success/recovery/human-intervention architecture evidence with source scope; quarantine latency/token economic claims until reconciled.
